newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Spanish general leads Guatemala U.N. peacekeepers.
newsitem.headline: Spanish general leads Guatemala U.N. peacekeepers.

text.p: A Spanish general was named on Friday to head the 155 U.N. peacekeepers who will monitor the implementation of Guatemala's recent accords that ended 36 years of civil war.

Brigadier-General Jose B. Rodriguez, who commanded the first Spanish contingent of U.N. peacekeepers in Angola, will begin employing the 155 military observers for Guatemala in February, U.N. spokesman Juan-Carlos Brandt said.

Under the Dec. 29 peace agreements, the Guatemalan army is to cut its numbers and about 3,000 guerrillas from the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) are to go to assembly points, disarm and be integrated into civilian life. U.N. observers will monitor assembly points.
The Security Council voted on Jan. 20 to send the peacekeepers to Guatemala after China dropped its opposition prompted by the Central American country's ties to Taiwan.
Diplomats said Guatemala had agreed not to openly support moves aimed at securing U.N. membership for Taiwan. China regards Taiwan as a renegade province.
